issue_context.title: System.Runtime.InteropServices.MarshalDirectiveException pops up when executing MetaFile automation case
issue_context.body:
### .NET version

**.Net 7.0 SDK:** 7.0.100-preview.5.22227.7

### Did it work in .NET Framework?

No

### Did it work in any of the earlier releases of .NET Core or .NET 5+?

Yes, it is a regression issue, cannot repro in .Net 6.0

### Issue description

System.Runtime.InteropServices.MarshalDirectiveException
  HResult=0x80131535
  Message=Cannot marshal 'parameter # 5': Cannot marshal managed types when the runtime marshalling system is disabled.
  Source=<Cannot evaluate the exception source>
  StackTrace:
<Cannot evaluate the exception stack trace>

  This exception was originally thrown at this call stack:
    [External Code]
    WinFormsApp12.Form1.Form1() in Form1.cs
    WinFormsApp12.Program.Main() in Program.cs

### Steps to reproduce

[WinFormsApp12.zip](https://github.com/dotnet/winforms/files/8582038/WinFormsApp12.zip)
1. Put tested application to the C:\Test folder on test machine
2. Open that test application, build and run
comments: It seems not a Winforms issue, please triage
@kant2002 could this be a fallout from of the comwrapper related changes?

I think not. `Cannot marshal managed types when the runtime marshalling system is disabled.` this message indicates to me that `DisableRuntimeMarshalling` attribute applied to `System.Windows.Forms` assembly. I would guess that SDK automatically insert that attribute for some reasons (trimming for example).

LibraryImportGenerator would solve this kind of issues one and for all.

Exception happens which I see when run with Debug mode is following
 
```
System.Runtime.InteropServices.ExternalException: 'A generic error occurred in GDI+.'
   at System.Drawing.Imaging.Metafile..ctor(String filename)
   at WinFormsApp12.Form1..ctor() in C:\Users\kant\Downloads\WinFormsApp121\WinFormsApp12\Form1.cs:line 12
   at WinFormsApp12.Program.Main() in C:\Users\kant\Downloads\WinFormsApp121\WinFormsApp12\Program.cs:line 14
```
```
>dotnet --info
.NET SDK:
 Version:   7.0.100-preview.5.22227.8
 Commit:    36f0f64cf5
```

Oops, sorry. I repro reported error
```
This exception was originally thrown at this call stack:
    System.Drawing.SafeNativeMethods.Gdip.GdipEnumerateMetafileDestPointI(System.Runtime.InteropServices.HandleRef, System.Runtime.InteropServices.HandleRef, ref System.Drawing.Point, System.Drawing.Graphics.EnumerateMetafileProc, System.IntPtr, System.Runtime.InteropServices.HandleRef)
    System.Drawing.Graphics.EnumerateMetafile(System.Drawing.Imaging.Metafile, System.Drawing.Point, System.Drawing.Graphics.EnumerateMetafileProc, System.IntPtr, System.Drawing.Imaging.ImageAttributes)
    System.Drawing.Graphics.EnumerateMetafile(System.Drawing.Imaging.Metafile, System.Drawing.Point, System.Drawing.Graphics.EnumerateMetafileProc)
    WinFormsApp12.Form1.Form1() in Form1.cs
    WinFormsApp12.Program.Main() in Program.cs
```

but again, I see that issue should belongs to dotnet/runtime

Yes it should. We recently discovered support for this in our analyzer. See https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn-analyzers/issues/5995

/cc @jkoritzinsky @elinor-fung

In the latest .Net 7.0 build: 7.0.100-preview.6.22310.18, the exception is changed as following:

System.ArgumentNullException
  HResult=0x80004003
  Message=Value cannot be null.
  Source=System.Private.CoreLib
  StackTrace:
   at System.ArgumentNullException.Throw(String paramName)
   at System.Runtime.InteropServices.Marshal.GetDelegateForFunctionPointer[TDelegate](IntPtr ptr)
   at System.Drawing.Graphics.EnumerateMetafileProcMarshaller.<>c__DisplayClass3_0.<.ctor>b__0(EmfPlusRecordType recordType, Int32 flags, Int32 dataSize, IntPtr data, IntPtr callbackData)
   at System.Drawing.SafeNativeMethods.Gdip.<GdipEnumerateMetafileDestPointI>g____PInvoke|541_0(IntPtr graphics, IntPtr metafile, Point* destPoint, IntPtr callback, IntPtr callbackdata, IntPtr imageattributes)
   at System.Drawing.SafeNativeMethods.Gdip.GdipEnumerateMetafileDestPointI(HandleRef graphics, HandleRef metafile, Point& destPoint, EnumerateMetafileProc callback, IntPtr callbackdata, HandleRef imageattributes)
   at System.Drawing.Graphics.EnumerateMetafile(Metafile metafile, Point destPoint, EnumerateMetafileProc callback, IntPtr callbackData, ImageAttributes imageAttr)
   at System.Drawing.Graphics.EnumerateMetafile(Metafile metafile, Point destPoint, EnumerateMetafileProc callback)
   at WinFormsApp12.Form1..ctor() in C:\Test\WinFormsApp12\WinFormsApp12\Form1.cs:line 21
   at WinFormsApp12.Program.Main() in C:\Test\WinFormsApp12\WinFormsApp12\Program.cs:line 14
Verified this issue in the latest .Net 7.0 SDK build from main branch: 7.0.100-preview.7.22330.8, it is fixed: no exception pops up, case passed.

review_comments: Rather than using `!` here, should EnumerateMetafileProc be declared to take a `PlayRecordCallback?` rather than a `PlayRecordCallback`?
I think so, but that's a public API change and I wanted to make sure we got this fix in before .NET 7 ships as this is causing compatibility breaks.
We should do both in 7 :)  If you don't want to do it here, can you please open a separate PR for it?  Thanks.
I'll open another PR for that once I merge this one in. 👍
